title: Construction 2: Perpendicular bisector of a segment (compass and straight edge only)
show: compass-and-straight-edge construction: segment AB 8 cm with the arcs and the perpendicular bisector, with arcs left visible

example.question: Draw a segment $[AB]$ with $|AB| = 8$ cm. Using only a compass and straight edge, construct the perpendicular bisector of $[AB]$.

steps.say: Open the compass to more than half of $|AB|$, about $5$ cm. Put the point on $A$ and draw an arc above and below the segment.

rows.aside: Do not change the setting until both arcs are drawn.

steps.say: Keep the same setting. Put the point on $B$ and draw an arc above and below the segment, crossing the first two arcs.

rows.aside: The arcs cross at two points, one above $[AB]$ and one below.

steps.say: With the ruler, draw a straight line through the two crossing points. Mark where it cuts $[AB]$ and call that point $M$.

rows.aside: Leave every arc on the page. They are your construction lines and the marks are tied to them.
$|AM| = |MB| = 4$ cm and the line meets $[AB]$ at $90^\circ$.

title: Construction 10: Triangle given three sides (SSS)
show: compass-and-straight-edge construction: triangle with sides 7, 6, 4 cm built by arcs, with arcs left visible

example.question: Construct the triangle $ABC$ with $|BC| = 7$ cm, $|AB| = 6$ cm and $|AC| = 4$ cm.

steps.say: Sketch a rough triangle first and write the three lengths on it. This is the plan for the construction.

rows.aside: A labelled pilot diagram earns marks even if the construction goes wrong.

steps.say: With the ruler, draw $[BC]$ with $|BC| = 7$ cm. Label $B$ and $C$.

rows.aside: Measure from the $0$ mark, not from the end of the ruler.

steps.say: Set the compass to $6$ cm. Put the point on $B$ and draw an arc above $[BC]$.

rows.aside: This arc holds every point that is $6$ cm from $B$.

steps.say: Set the compass to $4$ cm. Put the point on $C$ and draw an arc that crosses the first one. Label the crossing $A$.

rows.aside: $A$ is $6$ cm from $B$ and $4$ cm from $C$.

steps.say: Join $A$ to $B$ and $A$ to $C$ with the ruler. Leave both arcs on the page.

rows.aside: Check $|AB| = 6$ cm and $|AC| = 4$ cm with the ruler.

title: Construction 11: Triangle given SAS data
show: compass-and-straight-edge construction: triangle with AB 6, BC 8 and angle B 70°, with arcs left visible

example.question: Construct the triangle $ABC$ with $|AB| = 6$ cm, $|BC| = 8$ cm and $|\angle ABC| = 70^\circ$.

steps.say: Sketch a rough triangle and write $6$ cm, $8$ cm and $70^\circ$ on it, with the angle at $B$.

rows.aside: The angle sits between the two given sides, so it goes at $B$.

steps.say: With the ruler, draw $[BC]$ with $|BC| = 8$ cm. Label $B$ and $C$.

rows.aside: Measure from the $0$ mark on the ruler.

steps.say: Put the protractor centre on $B$ with its base line along $[BC]$. Mark a dot at $70^\circ$. Draw a ray from $B$ through the dot.

rows.aside: Read the scale that starts at $0^\circ$ on $[BC]$.

steps.say: On the ray, measure $6$ cm from $B$. Mark the point $A$.

rows.aside: Make an arc or a clear mark so the $6$ cm can be seen.

steps.say: Join $A$ to $C$ with the ruler. Label all three vertices.

rows.aside: Leave the angle mark and the arc on the page.

title: Construction 12: Triangle given ASA data
show: compass-and-straight-edge construction: triangle with BC 8 cm and angles 40° and 65°, with arcs left visible

example.question: Construct the triangle $ABC$ with $|BC| = 8$ cm, $|\angle B| = 40^\circ$ and $|\angle C| = 65^\circ$.

steps.say: Sketch a rough triangle. Write $8$ cm on $[BC]$, $40^\circ$ at $B$ and $65^\circ$ at $C$.

rows.aside: Label the vertices now so you do not lose marks later.

steps.say: With the ruler, draw $[BC]$ with $|BC| = 8$ cm. Label $B$ and $C$.

rows.aside: The side is between the two angles, so both angles sit on it.

steps.say: Put the protractor centre on $B$ with its base line along $[BC]$. Mark $40^\circ$ and draw a ray from $B$ through the mark.

rows.aside: Read the scale that starts at $0^\circ$ on $[BC]$.

steps.say: Put the protractor centre on $C$ with its base line along $[CB]$. Mark $65^\circ$ and draw a ray from $C$ through the mark.

rows.aside: Now the base line points the other way, so start again from $0^\circ$ on $[CB]$.

steps.say: The two rays cross at one point. Label it $A$.

rows.aside: Leave the angle marks on the page.

title: Construction 3: Line perpendicular to a line l through a point not on l
show: compass-and-straight-edge construction: line l, external point P, arcs and the perpendicular through P, with arcs left visible

example.question: Draw a line $l$ and mark a point $P$ above it. Construct the line through $P$ perpendicular to $l$.

steps.say: Put the compass point on $P$. Open it wider than the distance from $P$ to $l$. Draw an arc that cuts $l$ in two places. Call them $A$ and $B$.

rows.aside: Now $|PA| = |PB|$, because both are the radius of the same arc.

steps.say: Put the compass point on $A$ and draw an arc below $l$. Keep the same setting. Put the point on $B$ and draw a second arc that crosses the first. Call the crossing $Q$.

rows.aside: Any setting works, as long as the two arcs cross.

steps.say: With the ruler, draw a straight line from $P$ to $Q$.

rows.aside: This line meets $l$ at $90^\circ$.
Leave every arc on the page. They are the construction lines.

title: Construction 5: Line parallel to a given line through a given point
show: compass-and-straight-edge construction: line l, external point P, parallel line through P, with arcs left visible

example.question: Draw a line $l$ and mark a point $P$ above it. Construct the line through $P$ parallel to $l$.

steps.say: Pick a point $A$ on $l$. With the ruler, draw a line through $A$ and $P$, and extend it beyond $P$.

rows.aside: This line crosses $l$ and passes through $P$.

steps.say: Put the compass point on $A$ and draw an arc that cuts $l$ at $B$ and the transversal at $C$.

rows.aside: Do not change the compass setting.

steps.say: Put the compass point on $P$. With the same setting, draw an arc that cuts the transversal at $D$. Measure the distance $|BC|$ with the compass.

rows.aside: Then, with the point on $D$, mark that distance on the arc to find $E$, on the same side as $B$.

steps.say: With the ruler, draw a line through $P$ and $E$.

rows.aside: The angle at $P$ equals the angle at $A$. They are corresponding angles, so $PE \parallel l$.
